what_this_part_is: `condition_posterior_on_predictive_admission` is meant to fail closed above a declared budget, and it accepts ANY finite non-negative budget: at 1.0 it conditions away 99.9997% of the posterior, renormalizing by 3.4e5, and returns an ordinary `PosteriorGrid` with the same dataset id, the original admissible mask (so the summary reports admissible_fraction 1.0) and no field recording that anything happened. The audit is a separate object bound to it by no digest, and every PosteriorGrid-accepting UQ function takes `.posterior`. R-71's two findings -- the forward-table constructor and the source-result binding -- are parts B and C.
reach: LIBRARY_ONLY. `engcore.uq` is public API and the only in-repo callers are experiments/kinetics_k31 and k4, both of which declare a budget of 1e-12. No MCP entry point conditions a posterior.

what_was_already_seen.R-59, from the audit: 'budget=0.05: REFUSED' / 'budget=1.0: ACCEPTED unsupported_mass=0.999997 supported=2.973e-06 factor=3.363e+05' / 'budget=5.0: ACCEPTED' / 'type: PosteriorGrid dataset_id: fit-data-v1 (same as original: True)' / 'fields carrying the conditioning: []' / and the summary still reporting full admissibility. In the reproduction the conditioned posterior's standard deviation jumps from 0.1 to 0.5 and its 95% interval becomes the two tail nodes, while nothing in the record it hands on says so.

a_budget_is_a_bound_and_the_core_has_a_m.rule: New module constant `MAXIMUM_CONDITIONED_UNSUPPORTED_MASS = 0.05`. `PredictiveAdmissionAudit` and `condition_posterior_on_predictive_admission` refuse a declared budget above it, naming the constant.
a_budget_is_a_bound_and_the_core_has_a_m.why: The budget says how much posterior mass a caller is willing to condition away and still call the result a posterior for the same question. 0.05 is not a new number: it is the complement of the 95% coverage every credible interval in this repository is declared at, so the rule is 'a conditioning may not discard more mass than the entire tail a 95% claim already excludes'. Above that the conditioned record is a statement about a minority of the original mass -- at the audited 1.0 it was a statement about 3e-6 of it -- and calling that the posterior is the false-confidence shape this round is about. A caller who genuinely wants to condition on a rare event is refused rather than served silently: what they want is a different question, asked with the observations that support it. Both in-repo callers declare 1e-12, so nothing in the tree moves.
a_budget_is_a_bound_and_the_core_has_a_m.closes: the budget half of R-59: 1.0 and 5.0 stop being admissible declarations.

a_conditioned_posterior_says_it_is_condi.rule: When conditioning actually happens (unsupported mass > 0), the returned `PosteriorGrid` carries a DERIVED dataset identity -- `f"{dataset_id}|predictive-admitted:{digest}"`, where the digest is over the admitted mask, the supported mass and the rejected point indices -- and its `admissible_mask` is the original mask AND the predictive-admitted mask, so a summary can no longer report full admissibility over nodes the conditioning removed.
a_conditioned_posterior_says_it_is_condi.why: A conditioned posterior is a different posterior: it answers 'given predictive admission', and it was indistinguishable from the unconditioned fit to the same dataset. The dataset identity is the field every downstream route reads to decide what a posterior is about, which is exactly why the marking belongs there and why re-using the original identity is what let a truncated record travel unnoticed. The mask is not cosmetic either: `admissible_fraction` is what a reader consults to find out how much of the support carried mass. Nothing numeric is chosen; the digest is over the record's own arrays.
a_conditioned_posterior_says_it_is_condi.closes: the unmarked-record half: a consumer that takes `.posterior` can tell, and so can anything comparing dataset identities.

the_audit_is_bound_to_the_weights_it_des.rule: `PredictiveAdmissionAudit` gains a trailing `conditioned_weights_digest: str = ""`, written when conditioning happened, and `ConditionedPosterior.__post_init__` refuses a pair whose audit digest is not the digest of the posterior's own weights (and refuses a non-empty digest beside an unconditioned posterior).
the_audit_is_bound_to_the_weights_it_des.why: The audit is the record that says how much mass was discarded and by what factor, and it was bound to the posterior by nothing at all: the two could be recombined freely, and an audit describing a 1e-12 conditioning could travel beside a posterior conditioned by 3.4e5. A digest over the weights is the one thing that makes the pair inseparable, and it is integrity-only in the usual way -- which is why the mask and the identity above are re-derived rather than asserted.

MAXIMUM_CONDITIONED_UNSUPPORTED_MASS.why: the complement of the 95% coverage this repository's credible intervals are declared at: a conditioning may not discard more mass than a 95% claim's whole excluded tail. Both in-repo callers declare 1e-12, twelve orders below it.

what_is_added: a trailing `conditioned_weights_digest` field with an empty default on `PredictiveAdmissionAudit`, written only when conditioning happened
a `__post_init__` on `ConditionedPosterior` (new behaviour, no new field)
what_is_not_changed: no existing field, default or enum member; no signature change
an unconditioned pass-through (unsupported mass exactly zero) returns the original posterior object, unmarked, exactly as now -- nothing was conditioned
the mass accounting, the 1e-12 sum contract and the refusal messages above the budget
compatibility.records_that_already_exist: No committed JSON carries a predictive admission audit or a conditioned posterior; the only files naming the record are the API snapshots, whose tests fail by design until the V4 round. Both in-repo callers (experiments/kinetics_k31, kinetics_k4) declare a budget of 1e-12 and their committed evidence records no conditioning.
compatibility.deliberate_narrowing: A budget above 0.05 stops being declarable, and a conditioned posterior stops being byte-identical to the unconditioned one -- which is the point. An audit and a posterior that were not produced together stop being combinable.

residuals_stated_in_advance: The digest is integrity-only, as every digest in this tree is: a forger who edits the weights can recompute it. What it closes is the accidental recombination and the silent hand-off, not a determined edit -- and the mask and the derived identity are re-derived from the arrays rather than trusted.

The derived dataset identity is a string, so a consumer that only logs it gains nothing automatic. What it does guarantee is that any consumer comparing a posterior's identity with the dataset it was fitted to will not match -- which is what the audit asked for.

Conditioning still returns the ORIGINAL posterior object when the unsupported mass is exactly zero. That is not a silent case: nothing was discarded, the audit says so, and marking it would change records for a no-op.
